title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this sits in the 1981-82 notes on 'déploiement' (unfolding) of stratified spaces. On the previous page Grothendieck takes a stratified space X = X_0 ∪ X_1 ∪ X_2 (index poset 0<1<2) and removes open tubular neighbourhoods of the lower strata. This gives the truncated strata Σ_i = X'_i, which are manifolds with boundary or corners. It also gives the boundary pieces Σ_ij of the tubes of X'_i inside X_j, and more generally pieces Σ_{i0...in} indexed by chains of the poset. Each Σ_ij comes with two maps: a tube projection Σ_ij → Σ_i and an inclusion Σ_ij → Σ_j.

On this page he abstracts this into axioms for a three-stratum 'unfolded' datum.

Data: topological spaces Σ_0, Σ_1, Σ_2, together with closed correspondences Σ_01 ⊂ Σ_0×Σ_1, Σ_12 ⊂ Σ_1×Σ_2 and Σ_02 ⊂ Σ_0×Σ_2.

Definition: Σ_012 := (Σ_01×Σ_2) ∩ (Σ_0×Σ_12) ⊂ Σ_0×Σ_1×Σ_2. This is the fibre product Σ_01 ×_{Σ_1} Σ_12, i.e. the composite correspondence before projection.

The axioms:
(a) The image of Σ_012 in Σ_0×Σ_2 lies in Σ_02, i.e. Σ_12∘Σ_01 ⊂ Σ_02. The marginal note says this means Σ = Σ_0⊔Σ_1⊔Σ_2 carries a (pre)order relation lying over the order of {0,1,2}: transitivity of the incidence relation. One then gets a commutative diagram. Its bottom square (Σ_012 → Σ_12 over Σ_01 → Σ_1) is cartesian by construction. Some arrows are marked [l] = lisse: the projections Σ_012 → Σ_0, Σ_012 → Σ_01 and Σ_12 → Σ_1.
(b) The maps Σ_01 → Σ_1, Σ_02 → Σ_2 and Σ_12 → Σ_2 are injective and 'bandants'. 'Bandant' is Grothendieck's ad hoc word for a tame or collared embedding of a boundary-type subspace. By base change Σ_012 → Σ_12 is then injective and bandant.
(c) Σ_012 = Σ_02 ∩ Σ_12 (inside Σ_2), i.e. the upper square is also cartesian.
(d) Σ_12 → Σ_1 is transversal to the bandant embedding Σ_01 → Σ_1, which makes Σ_012 → Σ_12 bandant.
(e) Σ_02 and Σ_12 are transversal bandant parts of Σ_2, so Σ_012 ⊂ Σ_02 is bandant.
(f) Σ_01 → Σ_0, Σ_02 → Σ_0 and Σ_12 → Σ_1 are smooth fibrations (locally trivial). Hence the induced maps on Σ_012 are fibrations too.

A margin note says (f) should simplify by requiring that the diagram W_01 ← W_012 → W_02 be trivial over W_0, i.e. a fibrewise (link-wise) local triviality over the bottom stratum.

Purpose: this is a first attempt at the 'théorème de dévissage' announced in Esquisse d'un programme §5. The idea is that a tame stratified space should be equivalent to a combinatorial-geometric system of manifolds with boundary or corners indexed by chains of the stratification poset, glued by tube fibrations. Here this is worked out in the 3-stratum case as axioms on correspondences.
errors: The transcription line 'Σ_01 ⊂ Σ_01' must be Σ_01 ⊂ Σ_0×Σ_1, and 'Σ_012 = Σ_0×Σ_1×Σ_2' must be an inclusion ⊂, not an equality.
In (c) the intersection Σ_02 ∩ Σ_12 makes sense in Σ_2 (both are bandant parts of Σ_2), not in Σ_12 as written or transcribed.

In (f) the claim that 'Σ_012 → Σ_02' is a (smooth) fibration conflicts with (b)/(c), which make Σ_012 → Σ_02 an injective embedding. It is probably meant as Σ_012 → Σ_0, or as a fibration compatible over Σ_0. In any case it does not follow formally from (f) alone without a compatibility over Σ_0. Grothendieck himself flags this in the margin: '(f) devrait se simplifier...'.
Σ_02 → Σ_0 is listed as fibrant without the [lisse] decoration given to the other two maps; this is minor.

ideas.what: Unfolded description of a stratified space: truncated strata plus link/tube boundary pieces Σ_{i0..in} indexed by chains of the stratification poset, with projections and inclusions.
ideas.modern_name: Unzipping/déploiement; décollage (functor on the subdivision sd(P)); Thom–Mather control data; abstract stratified sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970) for control data and abstract stratified sets; Verona (1984); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzipping, 2017); Barwick–Glasman–Haine / Haine (décollages, 2018-20)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (only as a sketch: the 'dévissage' of tame stratified structures, without these axioms)

ideas.what: Condition (a): composition of incidence correspondences Σ_12∘Σ_01 ⊂ Σ_02, read as an order relation on ⊔Σ_i lying over the poset {0,1,2}.
ideas.modern_name: Topological poset / stratified space as a space with a continuous preorder over P (Alexandrov-type stratification map)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A) for spaces over posets

ideas.what: Cartesianness of both squares together with transversality and 'bandant' (collared) embeddings: the corner structure Σ_012 = Σ_02 ∩ Σ_12 as a transversal intersection of boundary faces.
ideas.modern_name: Manifolds with corners / ⟨n⟩-manifolds, systems of fibrations with faces

ideas.what: Fibration axioms (f): tube projections as smooth fibrations compatible along chains, with the suggested simplification of fibrewise triviality of the link diagram over the deepest stratum.
ideas.modern_name: Compatible tubular projections / Mather's commutation relations π_i∘π_j = π_i

missed.claim: Grothendieck's chain-indexed data Σ_{i0…in} (previous page) and its axiomatisation here as correspondences with cartesian squares is essentially the 'décollage' description of stratified spaces (diagrams on sd(P)^op) later used for exodromy, and the 'unzipping' of Ayala–Francis–Tanaka. These notes show he was formulating it point-set/geometrically around 1981-82. The modern literature generally does not cite these notes, only the Esquisse.
missed.quote: signifie que Σ = Σ_0⊔Σ_1⊔Σ_2 a une relation d'ordre au-dessus de [0,1,2]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit and motivation: it gives an explicit geometric axiom set (cartesian, transversal, collared, fibrant) for reconstructing a tame stratified space from its unfolding, which is the content of AFT-type reconstruction theorems.

missed.claim: The axiom set is visibly unstable (crossed-out clauses, an inconsistent fibration claim, a margin remark that (f) should simplify via fibrewise triviality over W_0). The general n-stratum version and the equivalence with stratified spaces are not completed on this page.
missed.quote: (f) devrait se simplifier, par la condition que le diagramme au-dessus W_01 ← W_012 → W_02 ... soit trivial sur W_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. The equivalence is now known in the conically smooth setting (Ayala–Francis–Tanaka) and the Thom–Mather setting, so this is mostly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working axiomatisation of the 'dévissage' of stratified spaces announced only sketchily in the Esquisse. The ideas match Thom–Mather control data, manifolds with corners and later décollage/unzipping formalisms, so nothing is mathematically new. Seeing the chain-indexed correspondence formalism explicitly in 1981-82 is a modest historical detail.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Σ_0, Σ_1, Σ_2 espaces top.' (espaces topologiques).
'Posons Σ_012 ⊂ Σ_0×Σ_1×Σ_2 ... = (Σ_01×Σ_2) ∩ (Σ_0×Σ_12)': the relation to the triple product is an inclusion.
Left-margin note reads roughly: '(a) signifie que Σ = Σ_0 ⊔ Σ_1 ⊔ Σ_2 a une relation d'ordre au-dessus de [0,1,2]'.
(d): 'Σ_12 → Σ_1 est transversal par rapport à l'injection bandante Σ_01 → Σ_1 (cela implique que Σ_012 → Σ_12 est aussi bandant)'.
(e): 'Σ_02 et Σ_12 sont des parties bandantes transversales dans Σ_2 (donc Σ_012 ↪ Σ_02 est aussi bandant)'.
